newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast products mostly lower ahead of APIs.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast products mostly lower ahead of APIs.

text.p: Most U.S. West Coast wholesale product prices eased midday Tuesday, as buyers waited on the sidelines for Tuesday's weekly inventory reports from the American Petroleum Institute (API), dealers said.

Activity faded in the western market a day after a fire shut Texaco's 9,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) alkylation unit at its Los Angeles area refinery, traders said. The unit remains shut pending an investigation into the fire's cause.
Sellers lowered spot prices to try to draw out buyers waiting on Tuesday's inventory. Meanwhile, NYMEX levels ended steady to slightly weaker on Tuesday.
"The buyers would like to see the inventories before they go out and spend their money," a broker said.
Wholesale prices for Los Angeles conventional grade gasoline eased, with offers down two cents a gallon from Monday to 75 cents.
Offers for CARB mandated Phase II reformulated gasoline edged up a half cent to 77.50 cents, but brokers said buyers did not put out bids, likely forcing sellers to cut prices.
Early Monday, CARB gasoline rose as much 2.75 cents a gallon on the refinery fire but faded late on lower NYMEX prices.
CARB grade diesel oil in L.A. trimmed a half cent to 73/74.50 cents, traders said.
San Francisco gasoline remained two cents under L.A. prices as demand remained static after heavy rains early this month.
